Thanks for the context — reviewed the draft and Nebula's redlines. Short summary and proposed next steps:

1) One-time surcharge vs. implementation credit
- Recommendation: swap the line-item "implementation surcharge" for a capped "implementation fee" defined in the Change Order and tied to hours in Exhibit B. That gives us a clear cap and traceability. If Nebula refuses, propose an implementation credit (discount applied to first post-migration invoice) as a compromise.

2) MSA Section 4.2 (escape clause) language
- Proposed insertion: "Notwithstanding Section 4.2, for the limited purpose of migration activities described in Change Order ##NBH-042##, Customer agrees to a one-time implementation fee not to exceed $XX,XXX, tied to substantiated migration hours and capped at 10% of the first monthly invoice post migration."
- Alternative softer language: add explicit rollback trigger and acceptance criteria in Exhibit A with an SLA credit cap (e.g., max two months' fees) so Nebula has a predictable remedy.

3) Rollback trigger and SLA credit cap
- Draft rollback trigger: failure to restore baseline throughput within 72 hours of migration completion triggers rollback. Implementation rollback will be executed during the next maintenance window and Redwood will issue SLA credits per Exhibit C.

4) Next steps
- I'll attach a tracked-redline with the MSA/Change Order edits (redline_suggestion_msasec4.docx).
- Tessa / Jordan: ask Nebula if they will accept a capped implementation fee or prefer the implementation credit. If they accept capped fee, legal is OK to move to DocuSign for the change order (I can prepare the DocuSign envelope).
